newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SE Asian buyers step back after USDA report - trade.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian buyers step back after USDA report - trade.

text.p: Southeast Asian grains and oilseeds buyers backed away from the market on Thursday after a bullish overnight USDA soybean supply/demand report spurred a sharp rise in Chicago futures, regional traders said.
Many buyers around the region are also only now returning slowly from the long Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Hari Raya holiday period, which lasted from February 7-10 this year.
"I certainly don't see Southeast Asian buyers stepping into the market with prices getting firmer by the minute," a trader for a U.S. commodity house told Reuters.
"Are people in Southeast Asia willing to pay these prices? I'd be very surprised if they do so."
Another dealer said: "People are not going to rush in. It's not right for them to buy when prices are so high."

He said regional firms are also closely monitoring the outcomes of a tender for 140,000 tonnes of soymeal in South Korea later on Thursday and another tender on Friday in Taiwan for a combined shipment of 25,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 5,000 tonnes of soybeans.
Traders said Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand currently have open positions for April shipment for one Handy-sized shipment of meal each.

Some of the buyers in these countries may be tempted to switch from U.S.-origin meal to Brazilian or other South American origin if the differential between the two sellers widens further in their favour.

The March soymeal contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed $5.10 up at $247.20 a ton after the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) supply/demand report on Wednesday showed a 15 million bushel cut in soybean ending stocks to 140 million bushels.
The CBOT March soybean contract peaked on Wednesday at $7.65-1/2 a bushel, the highest level since October 2, 1996.

Prices of U.S. soymeal coming into Southeast Asia were quoted by regional dealers at around $315-$317 a tonne C&F for April/May shipment against last week's $305-$310 a tonne C&F for March/May delivery.
Brazilian-origin meal was quoted at about $305-$307 a tonne C&F for April/May shipment, they said.
Indian soymeal, on the other hand, was seen at about $314 a tonne C&F on a Tweendecker, from $309-$311 a tonne C&F the previous week.
U.S. soybeans were being indicated at between $316-$320 a tonne C&F for April/May delivery against last week's $312-$316 a tonne C&F for March/May shipment, dealers said.
"The bean market has been quiet recently. People are just coming back from the holidays so nothing will move until possibly next week," a senior trader for a European commodity house said.
The price of U.S. corn coming into Southeast Asia also jumped in line with the recent rise in Chicago, traders said.
Buyers were hesitant in picking up any corn until they get a clearer idea if China will export any further quamtities of the staple in the first half of the year.
"Some people here want to take a look again at China's corn situation first," one dealer said.
U.S. corn was quoted by Southeast Asian dealers at around $145-$150 a tonne C&F from $140-$143 a tonne C&F a week ago.
